observation.visible_scene: A close, low-angle view of the rear and right side of a yellow double-decker city bus (badges 'MAN', fleet number '2965', slogan 'MOBILIDADE FLEXÍVEL', a white line-drawing of a suspension bridge and buildings on the rear window, and a vertical column of three blue accessibility icons). A round red tail light and a small red side marker are lit. To the left are weathered pale building facades with framed windows; to the right a building with iron balconies, a distant church tower and a construction crane under a clear blue sky. A pedestrian is partly visible at the far right edge.
visible_changes: Over the ~1.3 s excerpt the bus image shifts gradually rightward within the frame (the 'MAN' logo, the icon column and the tail-light cluster all move right by a similar amount), while the bus's size, shape and orientation stay constant.

The nearer left-hand building shows only a small corresponding rightward shift, and the far background (sky, crane, church tower, right building edge) remains essentially fixed, producing a parallax pattern in which the closest object (the bus) moves most.
The red tail light and red side marker remain illuminated throughout; no change in brightness or state.
The bridge line-drawing, text and icons remain legible and unchanged in form, merely translated with the bus.
The drift is slow and continuous across the frames, already underway at the first frame and still ongoing at the last (no start or stop is captured).
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the bus is parked or in motion, and whether the apparent drift is caused by the camera translating (e.g. handheld or on a moving platform) rather than the bus moving.
What precedes or follows this excerpt (the segment is temporally cropped at both ends).
The identity of the pedestrian at the right edge and any activity around the bus.
uncertain_details: The exact cause of the rightward drift is not fully disambiguated: the constant bus scale argues against the bus driving toward/away, and the larger shift of the nearest object versus the smaller shift of the left building is consistent with camera translation/parallax, but a very slow lateral bus movement cannot be entirely excluded.
Small apparent position changes of the left building may be measurement noise or slight camera motion rather than true scene movement.
The magnitude of the drift is modest and partly plateaus between frames.

trace.prompt:
Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.
These are chronological samples of a TEMPORALLY CROPPED SEGMENT of a longer source video.
Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
